name: Bardeen
tagline: Browser-based AI automation for web scraping and repetitive tasks
painPoints: Browser extension model limits automation to browser-based tasks
Cannot manage email, calendar, or tasks as a full AI assistant
AI features focus on playbooks, not proactive personal assistance
Limited to what is visible in the browser — no deep system integration
Pricing escalates for advanced AI automation features
metaDescription: Looking for a Bardeen alternative? GAIA is source-available AI that triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across your tools. Self-hostable.
whyPeopleLook: Bardeen is clever for browser-based automation — scraping web data, automating repetitive click sequences, and triggering playbooks from browser context. But its browser extension model means it has no awareness of your email notifications, calendar conflicts, or task deadlines unless you are actively browsing those pages. Users who want an always-on AI assistant that proactively manages their productivity — not just a browser automation tool — look beyond Bardeen.
gaiaReplaces: Email-to-task automation replacing manual browser-based workflows
Calendar management outside the browser context
Proactive alerts and notifications without requiring browser activity
Cross-tool automation via MCP beyond what browser automation can reach
gaiaAdvantages: System-level integration beyond what a browser extension can access
Proactive by design: works in the background without you opening a browser
Full personal productivity stack: email, calendar, tasks, and memory
Flat monthly price without credit-based pricing
migrationSteps: Identify which Bardeen playbooks handle email, calendar, or task workflows
Recreate those as GAIA workflows with deeper tool integration
Keep Bardeen for browser-specific scraping and web automation tasks
Use GAIA as your primary AI assistant for personal productivity

faqs.question: Does GAIA do browser automation like Bardeen?
faqs.answer: GAIA does not perform browser automation or web scraping. Its strength is deep integration with specific tools — Gmail, Google Calendar, Todoist, and many others — rather than generic browser control.

faqs.question: Can GAIA and Bardeen be used together?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bardeen for browser automation and GAIA for personal AI assistance complement each other well. Use Bardeen to scrape data and use GAIA to process and act on that data via workflows.

faqs.question: Is GAIA proactive unlike Bardeen?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA runs continuously in the background, monitoring your email and calendar and surfacing information proactively. Bardeen executes playbooks when you trigger them or set a schedule.

faqs.question: Is there a free way to use GAIA, like Bardeen's free tier?
faqs.answer: Bardeen has a free tier; hosted GAIA does not. It is a paid plan at ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month with no credit metering, built for everyday assistance across email, calendar, and tasks. Self-hosted GAIA is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs) without any feature restrictions tied to usage limits.

comparisonRows.gaia: System-level assistant across email, calendar, and tasks from any interface, not a Chrome extension bound to one browser
comparisonRows.competitor: Chrome extension that automates browser-based tasks and scrapes web data using AI-generated playbooks running inside the browser

comparisonRows.gaia: API-level actions across your tools instead of browser-UI control, so nothing breaks when a page layout changes
comparisonRows.competitor: Browser-UI automation and web scraping: controls the browser like a user would, meaning automations can break when page layouts change

comparisonRows.gaia: Native inbox triage and AI reply drafting in Gmail, not scraped email data feeding browser playbooks
comparisonRows.competitor: Can scrape email data from web-based inboxes or trigger email sends via browser automation; no native inbox triage or AI-driven reply drafting

comparisonRows.gaia: AI that acts independently across your tools, not a script generator waiting for your trigger
comparisonRows.competitor: Magic Box translates natural language descriptions into browser playbooks on demand; AI is used to generate and refine automation scripts, not to act independently

comparisonRows.gaia: Monitors your workflow in the background and surfaces insights unprompted, with no schedules to define
comparisonRows.competitor: Primarily reactive: automations run when you trigger them or on a schedule you define; the tool does not monitor your workflow or surface unsolicited insights

comparisonRows.gaia: Deep integrations reached through native connections and MCP, beyond what browser automation can touch
comparisonRows.competitor: Connects to 100+ apps (Airtable, HubSpot, Salesforce, Notion, and more) primarily through browser automation and web scraping; some native API integrations on paid plans

comparisonRows.gaia: Full calendar management with AI scheduling intelligence, working outside any browser context
comparisonRows.competitor: Can automate calendar-related browser tasks (e.g., scraping event data or filling forms); no native calendar management or AI scheduling intelligence

comparisonRows.gaia: Persistent graph memory carries context across tools and time, so reasoning compounds instead of resetting per run
comparisonRows.competitor: No persistent memory system; each playbook execution is stateless and context-aware reasoning across tools is not a core capability

comparisonRows.gaia: Runs in the background on web, desktop, mobile, and messaging apps, with no Chrome instance required
comparisonRows.competitor: Chrome browser extension only; automations require a running Chrome instance, limiting use to desktop and preventing mobile or headless execution

comparisonRows.gaia: Source-available and self-hostable via Docker: inspect the code instead of trusting a closed extension with your tabs
comparisonRows.competitor: Proprietary closed-source SaaS platform with no self-hosting option

comparisonRows.gaia: Hosted: paid plan at ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month; self-hosting free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs)
comparisonRows.competitor: Free plan with monthly credits; Basic, Premium, and Enterprise tiers with credit-based pricing.
